children: Amgen (AMGN) reported Q3 revenue up 8% to $10.365 billion and adjusted EPS of $6.45, topping estimates. It raised 2026 revenue guidance to $38.9–$39.7 billion and adjusted EPS to $22.90–$23.70.
Amgen reported strong third-quarter growth across Uplizna, Imdelltra, Repatha, Evenity, TEZSPIRE and BLINCYTO. Prolia and XGEVA sales fell amid biosimilar competition, while Tavneos edged lower.
Amgen is advancing Phase 3 trials of injectable MariTide for obesity, sleep apnea and heart disease. Initial results are expected next year; studies also test dosing four times a year.
Amgen said Phase 3 OASIZ-301 met its primary endpoint, with dazodalibep significantly improving Sjögren’s disease symptoms at Week 48. Full results are due at an industry conference in November.
Amgen’s average 12-month price target rose to $410.82 from $406.39, implying 11% downside from its Nov. 3 close. Analysts maintained a Hold consensus: 12 Buy, 19 Hold and 6 Sell.
Amgen (AMGN) said its Phase 3 study of TEPEZZA in Japanese patients with chronic thyroid eye disease met both primary endpoints. Safety matched the drug’s established profile.
Amgen (AMGN) said the FDA approved updated IMDELLTRA labeling, cutting monitoring after the first two doses from 22–24 hours to 6–8 hours in an appropriate health care setting.
